svg.text: How the proof cuts a cycle into standard pieces (schematic)
Paper, Sections 9–11 (subdivision, passage words, matching) and the saddle example of Section 1.2
Brown: a subdivision of the fixed square whose list of cell types
depends only on the degree. Blue: a periodic orbit. Red: cuts where
it crosses a boundary. A closed orbit crosses each transverse
boundary arc at most once, so the number of links is bounded.
(b) A passage near a saddle: ẋ = x, ẏ = −λy
Time spent in the box: L = log(1/r). Contraction exponent: W = λL.
As r → 0 the “clock” L blows up; if λ → 0 as well, W can stay bounded
or grow at a different rate. The paper’s passage models (additive,
one-clock, two-clock) track such separated scales together with their
